crime.value: Serial murder by ice pick; planned mass stabbing of hotel guests on top floor. Central question: Can the night clerk stop the killer before he reaches the victims?
crime.quote: I can go quietly from room to room, using this master key I found in the safe...there won't be any unnecessary uproar or bother.

victim.value: Seventeen female hotel guests, mostly in single rooms on the top floor of the Cragmore women's hotel. They are vulnerable because they are asleep and isolated.
victim.quote: I see there are seventeen guests on that floor, most of them in single rooms. That'll make it easier, you know.

closed_world.value: The Cragmore hotel for women—a locked, respectable establishment with a single night clerk on duty, no house detective, manager asleep on top floor. Bounded by locked doors and social propriety.
closed_world.quote: The Cragmore was run very much like the nearby YWCA; no male visitors were allowed inside the building after midnight, when the front door was locked.

culprit_and_motive.value: Robert Edward Lambeth, age 23. Motive: narcissistic hunger for fame and notoriety. He seeks to become 'the most famous man in the country—in the world' through mass murder.
culprit_and_motive.quote: in a few hours, Mr. Doyle—in a few hours I'll be the most famous man in the country—in the world.

investigator.value: Homer Doyle, the night clerk. He becomes the only person capable of stopping Lambeth, yet faces a moral crisis: stopping the killer will bring him modest recognition, but allowing the murders will make him famous as the man who took Lambeth's surrender.
investigator.quote: Doyle sat there in a sudden blinding agony of indecision...After all, not only the young have dreams of glory.
